name: tooltip
description: A hover/focus tooltip: add data-tooltip="..." directly onto any real element to give it one, no wrapper markup required. E.g. explaining why a disabled Undo button is disabled.

props.name: text
props.description: The tooltip's text. In real usage this is the data-tooltip attribute value on the actual trigger element (a button, an icon span, etc.) -- not a separate component instance. A line break in the text (a newline in the attribute value) starts a new line in the bubble, so one tooltip can carry a label, a text and a translation.

props.name: label
props.description: Only used by this component's own demo trigger (template.html): the visible content of the illustrative element data-tooltip is attached to. In real use, data-tooltip goes on an element the page already has; this prop has no meaning there.

props.name: preview
props.description: visible: data-preview="visible" on the [data-tooltip] element shows the tooltip without hover/focus. Documentation only (the site's Toasters and tooltips card); never in product UI.

props.name: data-tooltip-mode
props.description: On <html> or <body>, not on a trigger: 'layer' shows every tooltip on one fixed layer in <body> after a delay instead of the trigger's own ::after, so no overflow ancestor cuts it.

props.name: data-tooltip-delay
props.description: With layer mode: milliseconds before a tooltip shows.

props.name: window.dsTooltip
props.description: Layer mode only: show(box, text) shows host text at a box ({getBoundingClientRect}), e.g. a word inside a text; hide(); isTrigger(element); delay (ms).

rationale: Styled to Figma D_SYSTEM's Tooltip (node 103:4777): a dark fill (tooltip-bg, Figma base/900), a 1px tooltip-border, white body text, 10px padding, no shadow -- dark so it reads as a layer above the page in either theme. Pure CSS, no JavaScript: content: attr(data-tooltip) reads the trigger's own attribute, and :hover / :focus-visible are the whole show condition, because a tooltip's dismissal is exactly 'stop hovering or focusing'. Adding JS (as popup and dropdown-menu need for their open state) would be complexity with no functional gain. Figma's text+icon variant is not implemented: the bubble is the host's ::after, and a host's ::before is already taken (text-button's hover brackets), so there is no free box for an icon. Known limitation: no viewport clamping, so a trigger near a container edge can render the bubble partly off-screen. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Update 2026-09-30 (explicit request): the bubble is at most a third of the viewport wide and wraps, and a small component.js keeps it on screen -- shifted inside the viewport edges, flipped below when it only fits there, and its text cut at the last word that fits, with an ellipsis, when it fits on neither side. Show/hide stays pure CSS; the script only measures and sets --_tooltip-shift, data-tooltip-placement and data-tooltip-clamped on the trigger. Layer mode, 2026-10-23 (opt-in, so existing pages keep the immediate CSS bubble): the bubble drawn as the trigger's ::after is cut by any overflow ancestor (a scrolling table, a clamped cell) and covered by a sticky bar; one fixed layer sized to the trigger shows the same bubble above everything, with the same placement and shift logic. The delay keeps a page full of labelled buttons from flashing tooltips while the pointer crosses it. A text-button, header-tab or sort button whose label carries data-tooltip shows it for the whole button. window.dsTooltip (2026-10-23): a host that explains words inside running text (no element per word) shows its text on the same layer, so there is one tooltip mechanism and one look on the page.
a11y_notes: :focus-visible (not just :hover) shows the tooltip, so keyboard users reach it with Tab; so does keyboard focus on a control inside the trigger (:has(:focus-visible), 2026-10-03), for a tooltip set on a container such as a table cell around a button. The tooltip text is CSS generated content and is not announced as a description; if it must be announced, the host should add aria-describedby pointing at a real, visually hidden text node. A native <button disabled> can't receive focus, so a tooltip on a disabled button is mouse-only; to make it keyboard-reachable, the host would use aria-disabled on a still-focusable button instead of the disabled attribute.
